title: Distinctive Capillary Action by Micro-channels in Bone-like Templates can Enhance Recruitment of Cells for Restoration of Large Bony Defect
protocol: Cut PU sponges into bridge-shapes with dimensions of 3.5 cm in height x 5 cm in length x 1.5 cm in width.
Prepare a 4% (w/v) NaOH solution using a 150 ml beaker.
Immerse and squeeze the prepared sponges until they are completely soaked in the NaOH solution.
Place the beaker with the sponges in an ultrasonicator set at 42 kHz without heat for 15-20 minutes.
Rinse the sponges with distilled water for 5-10 minutes, squeezing and allowing them to expand during rinsing.
Remove excess water by squeezing the sponges with paper towels.
Dry the sponges in an oven at 60-80 °C.
Measure 10 g of nano-sized HA powder.
Prepare a beaker containing the magnetic stir bar, measuring its weight for calculation purposes.
Add 20 ml of distilled water into the 50 ml beaker.
Heat the solution for 120-140 °C and stir using a hot plate magnetic stirrer.
Add 0.3 g (3% w/w) of polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) per powder into distilled water while stirring at 300-400 rpm.
Stir until the PVA has completely dissolved.
Turn off the heat and add 0.1 g (1% w/w) of sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) for powder while stirring at 400-500 rpm.
Stir until the CMC has completely dissolved and cool down to RT.
Add 0.3 g (3% w/w) of ammonium polyacrylate dispersant per powder while stirring at 300-400 rpm.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Add 0.2 g (2% w/w) of glycerin per powder while stirring at 300-400 rpm.
Stir until completely dissolved.
Slowly disperse the HA powder into the solution while stirring at 600-900 rpm and keep stirring for 5 min.
Sonicate for 5 min using an ultrasonicator to ensure dispersion of any agglomeration of the HA powder.
Add an extra 5 ml of distilled water into the mixture while stirring at 600-900 rpm.
Heat the mixture at 90-100 °C and stir using a magnetic stirrer at 600-800 rpm to evaporate the water content.
Measure the whole weight including the beaker and mixture from time to time until a powder/liquid ratio of 1.75-1.8 is obtained.
Dry the HA coated templates for a minimum of 5 hours under cooling conditions (20-25 °C) with gentle air circulation.
Place the dried HA coated templates on an alumina crucible.
Heat the templates at 2 °C/min until reaching 230 °C.
Continue heating at 1 °C/min until reaching 280 °C.
Further heat at 0.5 °C/min until reaching 400 °C.
Increase temperature at 3 °C/min until reaching 600 °C.
Maintain the temperature at 600 °C for 1 hour.
Heat to 1230 °C at a rate of 5 °C/min.
Maintain the temperature at 1230 °C for 3 hours.
Cool down at a rate of 5 °C/min to room temperature.
Culture pre-osteoblastic MC3T3 cells in non-osteogenic media consisting of α-MEM, supplemented with 10% Fetal Bovine Serum (FBS) and 1% antibiotics (streptomycin and penicillin).
Add a cell suspension at a density of 2 x 10^6 cells/ml into a single well within a 6-well plate.
Place the bridge-shaped template vertically in the 6-well plate, with one leg immersed in the cell suspension and the other leg in an adjacent empty well.
Allow the template to absorb the cell suspension for 10 minutes.
Add 5 ml of media to the well originally filled with the cell suspension.
Replenish the medium in both wells every 2 or 3 days until 7 days have elapsed.
Fix the cells and scaffold by immersing in 100% EtOH for 20-30 min.
Stain with Hematoxylin for 1-2 min.
Rinse with distilled water for 1-2 min twice.
Dehydrate by immersion in 70%, then 95%, then 100% EtOH for 1-2 min each.
Stain with Eosin for 20-30 sec.
Rinse with distilled water for 12 min twice.
Dehydrate by immersion in 70%, 80%, 90%, and 100% EtOH for 1-2 min each.
Embed the scaffold in an acrylic resin for sectioning and imaging.
Determine cell viability using the MTT cell viability assay at days 3 and 7.
Conduct Live/Dead assay (Live/dead cell staining kit) at days 3 and 7.
